number_of_offences: Number of offences/counts charged: 2; Number of offences finally upheld: 0
key_evidence_accepted: The statements of the prosecution witnesses did not appear to be trustworthy, and the entire prosecution case was based on the telephone call made by accused-S, with no call details produced to verify its correctness. The recovery of the single barrel gun with the cartridge from the house of accused-L, the licence holder, was noted, but the prosecution failed to establish which accused used the gun.
witness_credibility: The statements of the prosecution witnesses did not appear to be trustworthy, and the witnesses turned hostile, denying statements and recoveries made in their presence.

legal_representation.accused: Ms. Ruchi Kohli, Ms. Babita Yadav, Amit Sharma, Ms. Srishti Mishra, R. C. Kohli, Advs.
legal_representation.state: Ms. Upasana Nath, Abhinav Mukerji, Ms. Radhika Gautam, Advs.

investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the dead body was recovered based on the disclosure statements made by the accused, and that the gun used in the crime was recovered from the house of accused-L, the licence holder. The prosecution also claimed that the postmortem report and forensic science laboratory report confirmed the use of the gun in the commission of the crime.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt, as there was no direct evidence as to who fired the fatal shot. The defence also highlighted contradictions in the statements of prosecution witnesses and the lack of verification of the telephone call made by accused-S.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that in a case based on circumstantial evidence, the prosecution must establish the circumstances fully and conclusively, and that the appellate court should not interfere with the trial court's acquittal unless the findings are perverse and not possible by any reasonable person.
precedent_relied_upon: Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra (1984) 4 SCC 116; Brajendra Singh v. State of M.P. (2012) 4 SCC 289; Chandrappa and Others v. State of Karnataka (2007) 4 SCC 415
